The property consists of 260 acres of uplands, 10 acres of wetlands, and a 45 acre lake.'; 'Camping Area Type of Facility: Primitive Camping Location of Facility: 37.82191 -99.92200 Primitive camping with vault toilet'; 'Picnic Area ... 37.82404 -99.91978 2 shelters with concrete pad, vault toilet'; 'Boat Ramp & Courtesy Dock ... 37.82535 -99.91965 Ramp may not be usable during low water periods.'; 'West Parking Area & Information Center ... 37.82499 -99.92232'; 'East Parking Area ... 37.82573 -99.91644'; 'Camping is allowed only in the designated camping area.'; 'Vehicles must stay on established roadways.'; Manager '(620) 895-6446'

KDWP camping page, Wayback capture of 2025-10-28 (https://web.archive.org/web/20251028091024/https://ksoutdoors.gov/Services/Outdoor-Activities/Camping); Wayback rate-limited my own fetch on 2026-11-06, so read from the copy of that same capture saved earlier today in batch p3-309: 'All campers and camping units at state fishing lakes or wildlife areas are limited to designated camping areas and a stay of not more than seven consecutive days ...'; 'Not all state fishing lakes and wildlife areas allow camping. For those that do, there is currently no cost to camp, but camping first-come, first served and reservations are not accepted.'

K.A.R. 115-8-9 as amended April 2023, Kansas Register Vol. 42 No. 14 (https://kssos.org/publications/Register/Volume-42/Issues/Issue-14/04-06-23-51015.html), read 2026-11-06: '(a) Camping shall be allowed only in designated areas on department lands and waters ...'; '(c) All campers and camping units at a state fishing lake or wildlife area shall be limited to a stay of not more than seven consecutive days on that department managed land unless otherwise established by posted notice or authorized by written permit from the department. Upon completing seven consecutive days on the same campsite, each person and all property of each person shall be absent from the department-managed area for at least five days.'

fees.source: KDWP camping page (Wayback 2025-10-28): 'For those that do, there is currently no cost to camp'; the Ford page (Wayback 2026-07-14) lists no fee. Read 2026-11-06

values.note: Free, first come; no reservations at Kansas state fishing lakes. Seven consecutive days at a state fishing lake, then five days away (K.A.R. 115-8-9(c), amended 2023); a longer stay needs a written KDWP permit.

booking.source: KDWP camping page (Wayback 2025-10-28): 'camping first-come, first served and reservations are not accepted', 'a stay of not more than seven consecutive days'; K.A.R. 115-8-9(c), Kansas Register 2023-04-06; the Ford page posts no different limit. Read 2026-11-06

facilities.source: KDWP Ford page (Wayback 2026-07-14): 'Primitive camping with vault toilet'. Read 2026-11-06

note: KDWP state fishing lake: a 45-acre lake on a timbered creek, 3 miles north and 5 miles east of Dodge City. One designated primitive camping area with a vault toilet, a gravel loop south of the picnic shelters; vehicles on established roads only. The boat ramp may be unusable at low water. --Claude
summary: KDWP Ford page (Wayback 2026-07-14): 45-acre lake, one designated primitive camping area with vault toilet at 37.82191,-99.92200; free and FCFS; max 7 nights (new). Pin ~330 m off -> move to the camping loop. Not waterfront kept. Phone missing -> (620) 895-6446. 'Goes dry' not on the page.
flags: PIN MOVE: stored 37.82485,-99.92108 is at the picnic/shelter grove ~330 m north of KDWP's camping-area point (37.82191,-99.92200). On Esri that point is beside the main gravel road, and the camping loop (a gravel loop with pull-in spurs) is just south-east of it; propose 37.8214,-99.9202 (loop centre), or KDWP's own 37.82191,-99.92200.

WATERFRONT: stored 'not waterfront' kept. The camping loop's east side is ~30-60 m from the lake through a belt of trees, and the lake level varies (KDWP: 'Ramp may not be usable during low water periods'; the north bay was weed-choked in the Esri capture). LAKEVIEW at best through the trees; when unsure, down.

DRY LAKE: the old note's 'Lake periodically goes dry' is not on the KDWP page, which only says the ramp may be unusable at low water. I reworded it to what KDWP says; the 'Ford SFL & WA' brochure (https://www.ksoutdoors.gov/home/showpublisheddocument/368/638941541871370000) stayed unread (KDWP 403, Wayback blocked or not archived).
PHONE missing (apply.py doesn't write it): propose (620) 895-6446 (KDWP area manager on the Ford page).
MAX STAY: newly written 7 nights (K.A.R. 115-8-9(c)). Hookups (none) left as stored. An old 4-H camp on the east side is a Boy Scout area (not public camping).
NOTE: dropped 'Site lengths not published' and 'Free, first-come, no hookups' (the fields hold it).
SAND: none - gravel loop on grass.
